news.headline: GLP-1 users report 4× more nail detachment — and more hair loss
news.summary: First controlled look, presented at the EADV Congress in Vienna: 575 GLP-1 users vs 1,329 never-users with type 2 diabetes or obesity (France, US, Brazil, Mexico). Nail detachment 39% vs 9%, nail discoloration 46% vs 17%; in the companion hair study, unusual hair loss 50% vs 34%, lost volume or density 42% vs 19%, and scalp redness about 3× as common. Cross-sectional and self-reported, and about half of users had nail problems before starting — an association, not proof. It lands on your two strongest lanes this week: the minoxidil cards and Tuesday's 'nail changes that are a red flag' card. No tracked creator's caption mentions it yet.
news.her_angle: 'On a GLP-1 and your nails are lifting or your hair is shedding? A dermatologist reads the new study'
news.source: HCPLive (EADV Congress 2026) — EADV release datelined Vienna, Oct 1

news.headline: Alopecia areata pill holds regrowth through two years
news.summary: Sun Pharma at EADV (company release, Oct 1): in the open-label extension of deuruxolitinib (Leqselvi) for severe alopecia areata, of the patients who entered the extension as responders and still held that response at week 52, 96.8% held it at week 108, and there were no deaths, clots or major cardiac events at the FDA-approved 8 mg twice-daily dose. Company-reported and open-label — but it sits on your hair-loss series, a week after baricitinib was approved for teens (Sep 25).
news.her_angle: 'Minoxidil won't fix this kind of hair loss' — alopecia areata, the autoimmune one, and the pills that now treat it

news.headline: Vitiligo pill plus light therapy: 59% reach face-repigmentation goal
news.summary: EADV, reported Oct 1: in the two Viti-Up phase 3 trials of upadacitinib (Rinvoq) for non-segmental vitiligo — 614 patients aged 12 and up — the share reaching 75% facial repigmentation kept climbing to 55.1% and 47.4% by week 76. In an 84-patient substudy, adding twice-weekly narrowband UVB got 59.3% there vs 37.0% on the pill alone. Approved in the EU in July; FDA review is ongoing — a 'what's coming' item, not a prescription yet.
